scenarios.name: Purchase on 20 November: the November token, exp 4 December; the window for December opens on 24 November.
Purchase on 27 November: the December token at once, exp 4 January. It is early until 1 December, which does not stop it creating a household.
(b) at once, when it has never applied a version 2 token to its current household (a legacy household, or a credential just entered); here E is an announced cut-over date.

A legacy household after the cut-over is announced: a device that holds no code shows "Enter your subscription code on one guardian device before <date>." (E more than 41 days away, or a value once seen more than 41 days away).
Otherwise it shows the ordinary notices (a device without a code, E never seen more than 41 days away).
Legacy household converted: on or after the cut-over it is lapsed, and the device claims with current: true first.
(c) The device picks a time evenly at random in the first 5 days, [E − 10 × DAY, E − 5 × DAY), and claims at its first run after that time.
(c) From E − 5 × DAY on it claims at its first run with no delay.

Monthly, renewal day the 28th, claim on 25 November: the November token again (a token whose exp is not later than E: it tries again a day later); after the renewal on 28 November it gets the December token.
Yearly, claim on 10 November: exp 4 December. The bound device claims again from 24 November (E − 10 days) and gets the December token.
A device that holds two tokens (this month's and an early one for next month) sends the one that is not early first, and the early one at the next write.

Household lapsed since 4 December, bound device back on 26 December: a claim with current: true gets the December token, which reopens the household; the plain claim that follows gets the January token, early, which extends it to 4 February.
(d) When its household is lapsed (E ≤ now, or a 402 lapsed), at once and with current: true — here a 402 lapsed while the device's own clock still puts E ahead.
Laptop closed from 25 December: it claims at its first run after reopening on 4 January, when the household is already lapsed.
payment-pending: show the reason with the way to fix it, then try at most once a day; "Payment problem" while E is less than 2 days away and once lapsed.
inactive: at most once a day; "Family has ended" only when a claim on this device came back inactive or revoked.
revoked: try at most once a day, or when the user asks.
429, 502, 503, no network: retry at later sync runs, with backoff (5 minutes, doubling, at most 6 hours).
replacement-used: show the date in retry_after. The subscription is still bound elsewhere: no automatic claim while E is in the future; once E has passed, one claim with current: true.
replacement-used: no "Renew on this device" until retry_after, and the notice shows that date; the bound rule goes on meanwhile.
bound-to-other-device, E in the future: no automatic claim — not by rule (b), not in the window, and no daily retry; "Renew on this device" only when E − now < 2 × DAY.
bound-to-other-device with no E (a version 1 household): no automatic claim.
bound-to-other-device: once E has passed, one claim without replace, with current: true; refused as bound, at most once a day while lapsed; stop if E moves into the future.
bound-to-other-device: once E has passed the old binding is usually stale and the claim with current: true binds this device without the rebind.
bound-to-other-device: a 402 lapsed also counts as E having passed.
bound-to-other-device is remembered until a claim succeeds, the credential is entered again or removed, or the device leaves: entering the code again claims by rule (b).
A code of an Institutions plan: the claim succeeds and the token's plan is not family; the client deletes the code, the claim secret and the token, and creates nothing.

No X-Sitr-Entitlement-Expires header: a version 1 household. With a code it claims once by rule (b) (the claim service not deployed answers like no network) and then not again while it holds that token; again only after the held token's exp has passed.
No X-Sitr-Entitlement-Expires header on a successful round after E was known: a version 1 household, never lapsed, no notice; a failed round without it changes nothing.
For a test household, (c) is instead "when E is less than 1 hour away" (strictly less: at midnight itself E is exactly an hour away); the 2-day notice does not apply.
unknown-code, wrong-product, invalid-receipt, test-purchase, family-sharing, bad-request: show the reason and stop until the user acts (also when lapsed).
